title: An approach based on data mining and genetic algorithm to optimizing time series clustering for efficient segmentation of customer behavior
tldr: Proposes a time-series-based customer segmentation method using genetic algorithm for feature weight optimization and spectral clustering, validated on 30 months of payment transaction data.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional static customer segmentation methods fail to capture temporal dynamics of customer behavior, leading to ineffective business strategies. Existing approaches neglect multivariate time series and cost as a key feature.
approach: Modeled each customer's behavior as a multivariate time series of purchase recency, frequency, amount, and customer lifecycle cost.
Applied a genetic algorithm to optimize feature weights, emphasizing the most discriminative dimensions.
Used spectral clustering on weighted features to segment customers into distinct behavioral groups.
Validated the method on 30 months of transactional data from a payment services company in Iran.
Compared against static segmentation baselines including K-means, fuzzy C-means, and hierarchical clustering.
findings: num: Spectral clustering with optimally weighted features significantly surpassed traditional static segmentation techniques.
Incorporating customer cost as a feature provides novel insights for customer analysis and business management.
Genetic algorithm optimization improved segmentation precision over equal-weighted feature approaches.
Time-series-based dynamic segmentation captures behavioral evolution that static methods miss.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces a genetic-algorithm-optimized time series clustering framework that captures temporal dynamics of customer behavior, overcoming the limitations of static segmentation. It demonstrates that incorporating customer lifecycle cost as a feature improves segmentation quality. The approach provides a methodological template for dynamic customer profiling using transactional data.
directly_justifies: Customer behavior should be modeled as time series, not static snapshots.
Genetic algorithm optimization of feature weights improves clustering quality.
Spectral clustering with weighted features outperforms traditional static segmentation.
limits: Single company dataset limits generalizability across industries and regions.
No evaluation on cold-start or new customer profiling scenarios.
Comparison limited to basic clustering baselines, not modern deep clustering.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was flagged as high relevance because the paper's core contribution is dynamic customer segmentation using behavioral time series data. Domain 3 (Expense Categorization) was considered but rejected because the paper segments customers rather than categorizing expenses. All other domains (1-4, 6-14) were rejected as the paper does not address demographics, financial practices, predictive modeling, budgeting, anomaly detection, mobile UX, privacy, or other topics. Borderline: Domain 5.B received medium because time series naturally captures dynamics but cold-start is not addressed.

limitations: Validation on a single payment services company dataset limits external generalizability.
Computational cost of genetic algorithm for feature optimization not analyzed. [unacknowledged]
remember_this: Time series clustering captures evolving customer behavior better than static methods.
Genetic algorithm optimization of feature weights enhances segmentation precision.
Spectral clustering with weighted features outperforms K-means and hierarchical approaches.
Customer lifecycle cost is an underexplored but valuable segmentation feature.
